content: 1. Kulier et al. (2011) conducted a systematic review on medical methods for first-trimester abortion, published in the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, highlighting the efficacy and safety of various approaches. 2. Kumar and Dogra (2009) discussed the diagnostic and management challenges associated with leprosy in the Indian Journal of Dermatology, Venereology, and Leprology, emphasizing the complexity of the disease. 3. Kumar, Dogra, and Kaur (2004) analyzed the epidemiological characteristics of leprosy reactions based on 15 years of experience in North India, as published in the International Journal of Leprosy and Other Mycobacterial Diseases. 4. Lambert et al. (2016) conducted a randomized controlled double-blind trial comparing cyclosporin and prednisolone in managing new Type 1 reactions in leprosy patients in Ethiopia, published in PLoS Neglected Tropical Diseases. 5. Lasry-Levy et al. (2011) performed a cross-sectional prevalence study in Mumbai, examining neuropathic pain and psychological morbidity in treated leprosy patients, published in PLoS Neglected Tropical Diseases. 6. Lockwood et al. (1993) described the clinical features and outcomes of reversal (Type 1) reactions in Hyderabad, India, in the International Journal of Leprosy and Other Mycobacterial Diseases. 7. Lockwood (1996) reviewed the management of erythema nodosum leprosum (ENL), discussing current and future treatment options in Leprosy Review. 8. Lockwood and Bryceson (2003) addressed the renewed use of thalidomide and associated concerns in the treatment of leprosy reactions, published in Leprosy Review. 9. Lockwood and Saunderson (2012) highlighted the ongoing challenges of nerve damage in leprosy for scientists, clinicians, and service providers in the International Health journal. 10. Lockwood et al. (2017) presented findings from the AZALEP trial, a randomized controlled study on azathioprine for treating leprosy nerve damage and Type 1 reactions in India, published in PLoS Neglected Tropical Diseases. 11. Maghanoy et al. (2017) conducted a prospective randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial on the effect of extended clofazimine treatment on ENL in multibacillary leprosy, published in Leprosy Review. 12. Mahajan et al. (1996) shared clinical experiences in studying pure neuritic leprosy, as published in the Indian Journal of Leprosy. 13. Mahmoud and Walker (2019) systematically reviewed adverse drug reactions associated with thalidomide in treating ENL, published in Leprosy Review. 14. Manandhar et al. (2002) linked high levels of inflammatory cytokines to poor clinical responses to steroid treatment and recurrent Type 1 reactions in leprosy, published in Clinical and Experimental Immunology. 15. Minuk et al. (2010) explored physician behaviors and ethical implications regarding access to thalidomide for multiple myeloma treatment in Canada, published in Current Oncology. 16. Naafs (2003) reappraised the treatment duration of reversal reactions in leprosy, advocating for a return to past practices, published in Leprosy Review. 17. Naafs (2006) questioned whether leprosy treatment is driven by science or politics, as discussed in Tropical Medicine and International Health. 18. Nabarro et al. (2016) reviewed the use of steroids and thalidomide in managing ENL over 17 years at the Hospital for Tropical Diseases in London, published in Leprosy Review. 19. Nashed et al. (2008) reported on intraneural corticosteroid injections for treating nerve damage in leprosy, including a case report and literature review, published in the Journal of Medical Case Reports. 20. Negera et al. (2017) conducted a case-control study on the clinico-pathological features of ENL at ALERT Hospital in Ethiopia, published in PLoS Neglected Tropical Diseases. 21. Nery et al. (2013) emphasized the importance of early diagnosis and treatment of Type 1 reactions in leprosy to prevent disability, published in Anais Brasileiros de Dermatologia. 22. Newbronner et al. (2017) summarized discussions from a multidisciplinary meeting on the legacy of thalidomide, held at the University of York, published in Birth Defects Research. 23. Newbronner and Atkin (2018) reviewed the changing health of thalidomide survivors as they age, published in the Disability and Health Journal. 24. Newbronner et al. (2019) surveyed the health and quality of life of aging thalidomide survivors in the UK, published in PLoS ONE. 25. Parle et al. (2018) examined the intersection of pharmaceuticals and statecraft in South Africa, focusing on opium, thalidomide, and contraception, published in Medical Humanities. 26. Pocaterra et al. (2006) analyzed the clinical course of ENL over 11 years in Hyderabad, India, published in the American Journal of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene. 27. Raju et al. (2014) studied serological responses to prednisolone treatment in leprosy reactions, focusing on TNF-α and antibodies to various biomarkers, published in Lipids in Health and Disease. 28. Rambukkana et al. (2002) demonstrated contact-dependent demyelination by Mycobacterium leprae in the absence of immune cells, published in Science. 29. Ramien et al. (2011) reported successful treatment of severe refractory ENL with the TNF inhibitor etanercept, published in Clinical Infectious Diseases. 30. Rao et al. (2006) conducted a multicenter double-blind randomized trial comparing three steroid regimens for treating Type 1 reactions in leprosy, published in Leprosy Review. 31. Raymond et al. (2013) systematically reviewed first-trimester medical abortion using mifepristone and misoprostol, published in Contraception. 32. Richardus et al. (2003) evaluated corticosteroid treatment for long-standing nerve function impairment in leprosy in a randomized controlled trial (TRIPOD 3), published in Leprosy Review. 33. Ridley and Jopling (1966) proposed a five-group classification system for leprosy based on immunity, published in the International Journal of Leprosy. 34. Rose and Waters (1991) discussed reversal reactions in leprosy and their management in an editorial published in Leprosy Review. 35. Samel et al. (2019) compared the life situations of women affected by thalidomide embryopathy in North Rhine-Westphalia, based on a recent cross-sectional study, published in BMC Women's Health. 36. Sales et al. (2007) conducted a double-blind trial comparing pentoxifylline and thalidomide for treating Type II reactions in leprosy, published in the Brazilian Journal of Medical and Biological Research. 37. Santos et al. (2017) explored the use of etanercept in treating ENL, published in Anais Brasileiros de Dermatologia. 38. Saunderson et al. (2000) investigated ENL reactions in multibacillary cases in Ethiopia, focusing on incidence and risk factors, published in Leprosy Review. 39. Saunderson et al. (2000) described the pattern of leprosy-related neuropathy in Ethiopian patients, including definitions, incidence, risk factors, and outcomes, published in Leprosy Review. 40. Saunderson et al. (2008) examined neuropathic pain in individuals treated for multibacillary leprosy more than ten years earlier, published in Leprosy Review. 41. Schreuder (1998) analyzed the occurrence of reactions and impairments in leprosy based on experience in northeastern Thailand, published in the International Journal of Leprosy. 42. Scollard et al. (2015) identified risk factors for leprosy reactions in three endemic countries, published in the American Journal of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene. 43. Sehgal et al. (1985) correlated morphological, bacteriological, histopathological, and immunological features of leprosy in a double-blind study, published in the Journal of Dermatology. 44. Serrano-Coll et al. (2018) reviewed direct and indirect mechanisms of Mycobacterium leprae-induced nerve damage, published in Pathogens and Disease. 45. Sheskin (1965) discussed the use of thalidomide in treating leprosy reactions, published in Clinical Pharmacology and Therapeutics. 46. Shiga et al. (2015) conducted a multicenter investigation of lifestyle-related diseases and visceral disorders in thalidomide embryopathy patients around 50 years of age, published in Birth Defects Research. 47. Singhal et al. (1999) reported on the antitumor activity of thalidomide in refractory multiple myeloma, published in the New England Journal of Medicine. 48. Smith et al. (2004) evaluated steroid prophylaxis for preventing nerve function impairment in leprosy in a randomized placebo-controlled trial (TRIPOD 1), published in BMJ. 49. Smith et al. (2009) predicted neuropathy and reactions in leprosy at diagnosis and before incident events, based on the INFIR cohort study, published in PLoS Neglected Tropical Diseases. 50. Srinivasan and Gupte (2017) discussed the management of leprosy reactions and prevention of disabilities, published in Leprosy Review. 51. Thangaraju et al. (2016) explored the role of etanercept in refractory ENL, published in the International Journal of Mycobacteriology. 52. Tio-Coma et al. (2019) identified RNA signatures in leprosy patients that predict reversal reactions before clinical onset, published in Nature Communications. 53. Toh et al. (2018) examined the diagnosis and impact of neuropathic pain in leprosy patients in Nepal after completing multidrug therapy, published in PLoS Neglected Tropical Diseases. 54. Upputuri et al. (2020) analyzed the use of thalidomide for treating ENL in an outpatient setting over five years, published in PLoS Neglected Tropical Diseases. 55. van Brakel and Khawas (1994) described silent neuropathy in leprosy in an epidemiological study, published in Leprosy Review. 56. van Brakel (2000) reviewed peripheral neuropathy in leprosy and its consequences, published in Leprosy Review. 57. van Brakel et al. (2003) emphasized the prognostic importance of detecting mild sensory impairment in leprosy in a randomized controlled trial (TRIPOD 2), published in Leprosy Review. 58. van Brakel et al. (2005) presented baseline results from the INFIR cohort study, investigating neuropathy and reactions in multibacillary leprosy patients in North India, published in Leprosy Review. 59. van Brakel et al. (2008) compared diagnostic tests for early neuropathy detection in leprosy in a large prospective study, published in PLoS Neglected Tropical Diseases. 60. van Veen et al. (2008) reviewed corticosteroid treatment for nerve damage in leprosy, published in Leprosy Review. 61. van Veen et al. (2009) evaluated interventions for ENL in a Cochrane systematic review. 62. van Veen et al. (2009) reviewed decompressive surgery for treating nerve damage in leprosy, published in Leprosy Review. 63. Voorend and Post (2013) systematically reviewed epidemiological data on ENL, published in PLoS Neglected Tropical Diseases. 64. Wagenaar et al. (2014) established normal threshold values for monofilament sensory tests in Indian and Nepali volunteers, published in Leprosy Review. 65. Wagenaar et al. (2017) compared five tests for early neuropathy detection in leprosy in field settings, published in Infectious Diseases of Poverty. 66. Wagenaar et al. (2017) compared the effectiveness of 32 versus 20 weeks of prednisolone in leprosy patients with recent nerve function impairment in a randomized controlled trial, published in PLoS Neglected Tropical Diseases. 67. Walker and Lockwood (2008) reviewed the management of Type 1 (reversal) reactions in leprosy, published in Leprosy Review. 68. Walker et al. (2014) analyzed mortality associated with ENL in Ethiopia in a retrospective hospital-based study, published in PLoS Neglected Tropical Diseases. 69. Walker et al. (2015) conducted the ENLIST 1 study, an international multicenter cross-sectional study of the clinical features of ENL, published in PLoS Neglected Tropical Diseases. 70. Walker et al. (2017) validated the ENLIST ENL Severity Scale in an international multicenter study, published in PLoS Neglected Tropical Diseases. 71. WHO Study Group (1982) provided technical guidance on chemotherapy for leprosy control programs. 72. WHO Expert Committee on Leprosy (1998) published its seventh report, providing updated recommendations for leprosy management. 73. WHO Expert Committee on Leprosy (2012) released its eighth report, addressing advancements in leprosy treatment and prevention. 74. WHO (2001) introduced the International Classification of Functioning, Disability, and Health, providing a framework for assessing health and disability. 75. Yamaguchi et al. (2012) reported a case of deep venous thrombosis and pulmonary embolism secondary to co-administration of thalidomide and oral corticosteroids in a leprosy patient, published in the Journal of Dermatology. 76. Zeldis et al. (1999) described a comprehensive program for controlling and monitoring access to thalidomide, published in Clinical Therapeutics. 77. Zhou et al. (2013) reviewed the transformation of thalidomide from a notorious sedative to a promising anticancer drug, published in Current Medicinal Chemistry.
